checks.name: required_audit_coverage
checks.detail: report covers all 8 Required Audit items with substantive answers
required_audit_items: What exact post-closeout evidence mismatch remained after `close-round` started succeeding, and which files showed it?
How was top-level `pytest_result.txt` rebuilt or refreshed so it contains only current-round command-plan-authorized command blocks and no stale prior-round commands?
How was `execution_log.json` regenerated so it agrees with `pytest_result.txt` and `command_plan.json` without stale prior-round commands or exit-code mismatches?

How were `codex_report_auto_summary.json`, `report_summary_synthesis.json`, and live `codex_report_summary` regenerated so `tests_ran`, `files_changed`, `generated_artifacts`, status, and acceptance recommendation agree?

How does final-check now prove `round_manifest_present`, archived report/pytest matching, generated archive coverage, command-plan authority, stale artifact IDs, Required Audit coverage, execution-log consistency, and report-auto-summary consistency all pass?

How does `run-closeout` now order close-round, archive creation, live artifact refresh, report-summary, report-auto-summary, and final-check so the accepted live state and archived state do not drift?
What regression tests prove post-closeout evidence refresh, archive/live agreement, stale command exclusion, real mismatch detection, log isolation, and command-plan authority remain correct?

How does this round preserve `run-round --execute`, `run-round --dry-run`, scoped closeout logs, command-plan authority, omitted-command blocking, policy-lint, policy-impact, prompt-doc immutability, and non-blocking historical/backlog sample artifact handling?
